answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place jobs or vote, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to have double-voted or failed a bonded task. Splitting one operator into a grove of fake agents does not multiply influence for free: every identity needs its own capital, which remains unavailable for other uses and can be destroyed by misconduct. A harbor of cheap accounts thus becomes costly to maintain, while the pigment of reputation accumulates only through verifiable work.
